sections.html:
Jefferson County sits in central Oregon high desert, and Madras is the county seat. Population reached 24,502 in 2020, a 12.8% jump over 2010. Jefferson was carved out of Crook County on December 12, 1914, and spreads over 1,791 square miles.

Two large blocks of land limit what can be owned here. The Warm Springs reservation, owned by the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs, takes up about 21% of county land, and the U.S. Forest Service manages about 24%. A parcel close to either boundary deserves a call to the Assessor about how that land is taxed, well before a sign goes in the yard.

Crooked River Ranch is the largest unincorporated community, a census-designated place with 4,912 people in southern Jefferson County, between the Deschutes and Crooked rivers near Lake Billy Chinook. Its roughly 12,000 acres make it the biggest homeowner association in Oregon.

Every house there answers to association rules and dues. Request the governing papers early so buyers read them up front instead of discovering them mid-escrow.

One office, the Finance Department, sends the bills and takes the money for every district that taxes Jefferson County property. You will find it at 66 SE D Street, Suite E, Madras. Assessment is a separate department, so questions about what your house is worth go to the Assessor, while questions about what you owe go to Finance.

The county's tax pages offer a form for changing your mailing address, a guide to reading the statement, foreclosure information and an appeal guide.

The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30. Bills are mailed by October 25. Installments fall on November 15, February 15 and May 15, and a date that hits a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day.

ORS 311.505 creates the discounts. Settle the whole bill in November and the county knocks off 3%. Send two-thirds and you get 2%. Send less and you get nothing.

A late account grows by 1.33% a month, or 16% a year, added on the 16th until the balance is cleared.

Selling in autumn? Settle in the contract who covers the November installment. Title will prorate it at closing.

sections.h2: How to pay and what it costs
sections.html:
Timing rules differ by how you send the money.

  • Mailed checks are on time if the USPS postmark is dated on or before the deadline (ORS 305.820). Address them to Jefferson County Tax.
  • A piece of mail without a postmark is judged by the day it is delivered.
  • Bank bill pay normally has no postmark, so plan for the funds to land on or before the deadline.
  • Point and Pay payments are timely if sent by 11:59 pm on the 15th.
  • At the counter you can use cash, check, money order or card.

Cards carry a 2.50% charge with a $2.00 minimum, a Visa Signature debit card runs $3.95 and an eCheck is $1.50. None of that goes to the county. The card line is 1-877-865-0432.

Read the county guide titled How to Appeal Your Property Value first. If you still disagree with the number, petition the Property Value Appeals Board by December 31, once your statement has arrived. Should that day fall on a weekend or holiday, you get the next business day. Phone Finance at 541-475-4458 to confirm the date and where to turn in the petition.

Unhappy with the board's order? The Oregon Tax Court Magistrate Division takes value appeals filed within 30 days of that order. If the issue is a denied exemption or a farm special assessment disqualification, you have 90 days.

Foreclosure follows a statewide rule. A parcel qualifies once its oldest unpaid year is three years behind. A list is drawn up in July and published in August. Paying the full tax and interest pulls a parcel from the list, though a 5% penalty attaches after publication.

After judgment the owner gets two years to redeem. An heir, a recorded lienholder or a city with a lien may also step in, paying the taxes, interest, penalty and a fee. If the house sells for more than the debt, the extra belongs to the owner.

You can still sell while owing tax. The usual sequence:

  • Request a year-by-year balance from Finance.
  • Hand it to the buyer's title company.
  • Escrow pays the oldest years first and takes the remainder out of your proceeds.

With a cash buyer there is no loan underwriting waiting on the payoff letter, so this step tends to move faster.

Acreage on a farm special assessment needs a closer look. If the land is disqualified, extra tax can be billed for up to 10 years, or five years inside an urban growth boundary. Get the status of every acre from the Assessor before you pick an asking price.

Country lots bring extra upkeep. Hard freezes put pipes and wells at risk, and strong sun with big temperature swings is hard on roofs and siding. The 2020 Santiam Fire burned in Jefferson County as well as Marion, Linn and Clackamas, so buyers may ask about wildfire.

Gather these before you ask for offers:

  • Your latest tax statement.
  • Well and septic records, if the lot is rural.
  • HOA papers, if the home is in Crooked River Ranch.
  • The special assessment status of any farm acreage.

Take the statement and a photo ID to the Finance office and ask for the balance on paper. Title companies want a written figure before they set a closing date. A balance still open that day gets paid out of your proceeds by escrow, so owing a little tax seldom kills a deal. A cash sale also avoids lender appraisals and repair demands, two usual reasons a rural closing slips.

Timeline matters too. If you want the November installment current before an offer comes in, pay it early or note the due date in your listing agreement so nobody is surprised. For well and septic records, start looking weeks ahead, since older rural files can be scattered between the county and prior owners. And if farm acreage is part of the sale, settle the special assessment question first, because it changes what a buyer might owe later.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Jefferson County, Oregon?
faqs.a: Madras. It was incorporated in 1911 and became the permanent seat after a 1916 election, replacing Culver as the temporary seat.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Jefferson County tax bill?
faqs.a: Walk in at the Finance Department, 66 SE D Street, Suite E, Madras, or pay by mail, by phone at 1-877-865-0432 or online through Point and Pay. Doors are open weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How much discount does Jefferson County give for early payment?
faqs.a: Paying the full bill in November takes off 3%, and two-thirds takes off 2%. Under two-thirds gets nothing.

faqs.q: What does late tax cost in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Interest of 1.33% a month, which is 16% a year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jefferson County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Escrow pays what is owed out of your proceeds. Ask Finance for a balance by year so the oldest years are paid first.
